description.summary: what the compositor decided about each output

protocol.description:
This protocol tells a shell component, such as the bar, the dock or the notification daemon, how the compositor treats each wl_output: the name it has in the user's settings, the shell surfaces the user wants on it, whether it is the primary or the focused output, what the display behind it can do, and the depth the compositor scans it out at.
The compositor resolves the user's settings and their defaults itself, so a client never has to match output names against the settings file. The description of a wl_output carries no serial number, so a client could not do that matching reliably.
Only privileged clients can bind the manager global. A compositor must not expose it to sandboxed clients.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the testing phase. Backward compatible changes may be added together with the corresponding interface version bump. Backward incompatible changes can only be done by creating a new major version of the extension.

interface.name: crownos_output_info_manager_v1
interface.description: A global factory for crownos_output_info_v1 objects.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager. Output info objects created through it are unaffected.

request.name: get_output

description.summary: observe how the compositor treats an output

request.description: Create an object that reports how the compositor treats output. The compositor sends every event of crownos_output_info_v1, followed by done, right after the object is created. Several objects may observe the same output.

interface.name: crownos_output_info_v1

description.summary: how the compositor treats one output

interface.description:
Reports how the compositor treats one wl_output. Right after the object is created, the compositor sends identity, shell, state, capabilities and scanout_depth, followed by done. After that, each change is a group of the events whose values changed, ended by a done event; the client applies the group atomically on done.
If the wl_output goes away, the object becomes inert: the compositor sends no further events for it, and the client should destroy it.

entry.name: focused
entry.summary: the output the pointer is on

entry.name: hdr
entry.summary: the EDID claims a PQ or HLG EOTF

entry.name: virtual
entry.summary: no display behind the output; a remote screen or a headless target

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the object. The compositor sends no further events for it.

event.name: identity

description.summary: the name the settings use for the output

event.description: The name that compositor.ron files the monitor under when no entry has its connector name: "MAKE MODEL SERIAL" when the EDID gives a serial number, else the connector name. A client that edits the settings of this output looks the entry up by the wl_output name first and by this name second, as the compositor does.

event.name: shell

description.summary: the shell surfaces the output shows

event.description: The shell surfaces the user wants on this output, with the defaults applied for each surface the user did not set: the bar on every output, the dock and notification popups on the primary output only. A client shows its surface on this output only while its bit is set. An output that is not part of the desktop, such as a hidden virtual output, has 0.

event.name: state

description.summary: the output's role in the desktop

event.description: Exactly one output is primary at a time; when the primary output goes away, the compositor selects another one and sends state for it. The focused bit moves with the focused monitor, the monitor under the pointer.

event.name: capabilities

description.summary: what the display behind the output can do

event.description: What the display behind the output can do, as the compositor reads it from the hardware. The compositor sends the event again if these values change.

event.name: scanout_depth

description.summary: the bit depth the output is scanned out at

event.description: The number of bits for each color channel that the compositor actually scans out to the display: 8 or 10. This can be lower than what the user asked for when the hardware refuses the deeper format. A nested compositor always reports 8.

event.name: done

description.summary: the end of a group of changes

event.description: Sent after a group of events, including the initial one, so the client sees them as one change.
